facts.statement: On Saturday 14 November 2026, SpaceX's Starship returned from space and was caught in midair by giant mechanical arms on the launch tower where its journey began 22 hours earlier: the first-ever capture of a Starship flying back from space.

source.title: SpaceX successfully catches Starship and makes history (The Associated Press, via NPR)

facts.statement: The upper stage soared into orbit, released 26 Starlink satellites, circled Earth 165 miles (265 km) up and completed 14 laps around Earth. It was SpaceX's 15th flight of a full-scale Starship since 2023 and only its second trip to orbit.

source.title: SpaceX successfully catches Starship and makes history (The Associated Press, via NPR)

facts.statement: Starship is the world's largest and most powerful rocket, 407 feet (124 metres) tall.

source.title: SpaceX successfully catches Starship and makes history (The Associated Press, via NPR)

facts.statement: The first-stage booster's engines stopped firing too soon on the way back down; its guidance sensed it was out of position and automatically diverted it to the Gulf of Mexico and self-destructed. SpaceX had already made three previous booster catches.

source.title: SpaceX successfully catches Starship and makes history (The Associated Press, via NPR)

facts.statement: SpaceX officials said the catch demonstrates the full reusability of Starship, intended for Moon and Mars travel; Starship is one of the landers NASA plans to use to put Artemis crews on the Moon.

source.title: SpaceX successfully catches Starship and makes history (The Associated Press, via NPR)

facts.statement: Starship Flight 15 (Ship 42 on Super Heavy Booster 22) lifted off from Starbase, Texas, at 4:47 p.m. CST (22:47 UTC) on Friday 13 November 2026.

source.title: Starship in orbit ahead of catch attempt, booster diverts to explosive splashdown

facts.statement: The photos show the Super Heavy booster returning to and being caught by the tower during Starship flight test 5 on 13 October 2024 (photos: Steve Jurvetson and others, CC BY 2.0), not the Flight 15 ship catch.

source.title: Wikimedia Commons: Starship flight test 5 booster return and catch (Steve Jurvetson, CC BY 2.0)

facts.statement: The spacecraft returned to its Texas launchpad by carefully lowering itself until two metal arms attached to the launch tower could secure it.

source.title: SpaceX successfully catches Starship and makes history (The Associated Press, via NPR)
